extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and policymakers interested in political theory, democracy, and national policy
extracted.subtask_description: Normative principles and evaluative criteria about the relation between democracy and nationality, and the duties of the democratic state (economic policy, social reform, national loyalty). Useful for assessing or designing democratic public policy and national organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: State duty to raise standard of living
rubrics_metrics.description: The American state can regain the loyal adhesion of economically less independent classes only by positive service — specifically by helping the wage-earner to conquer a constantly higher standard of living; it must recognize the legitimacy of his demand and make its satisfaction an essential part of public policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: growing industrialization produces distinct economic classes and stronger allegiance to unions than to the state. Failure to meet this duty risks the loss of democracy; the promise of economic freedom and prosperity to immigrants creates an additional moral obligation. Policy implication: state should actively promote higher living standards in ways that do not necessarily injure employers and that benefit general economic and social efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy's formative purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Democracy is not merely government by the people, majority rule, or universal suffrage; its chief formative purpose is to use democratic organization for the joint benefit of individual distinction and social improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a normative definition: democratic forms (machinery) are valuable insofar as they serve the higher purpose of fostering individuality and social betterment. Evaluations of democratic arrangements should ask whether they intentionally promote both individual excellence and social amelioration rather than treating such outcomes as accidental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy balancing individual and social amelioration
rubrics_metrics.description: Public policy should be intelligently informed by the desire to maintain a joint process of individual and social amelioration, keeping democracy sound by preventing permanent conflicts between small classes demanding special opportunities and the larger mass demanding generalized opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A binding and edifying public policy is required to avoid intensification of class and factional prejudices. When conflicts arise between the improvement of smaller versus larger classes, the criterion is whether policy sustains both individual distinction and broad social progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordination of democratic machinery to moral purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The machinery of democracy must be subordinated to its moral and formative purpose; such subordination demands a reconstructive programme and an efficient organization rather than leaving amelioration to happy accident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical consequence: evaluate institutions by whether their structures and policies are expressly and permanently responsible for ameliorating individual and social conditions. Anti-pattern: treating democratic institutions as neutral mechanisms without purposeful policy direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminate only against privilege
rubrics_metrics.description: The democratic state should never discriminate in favor of anything or anybody; it should only discriminate against all sorts of privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prescribes policy impartiality in favoring no special interests while actively opposing entrenched privileges. Evaluators should flag policies that create special favors or protected privileges as incompatible with this democratic standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: State assumption of functions and lawful redistribution
rubrics_metrics.description: A democracy cannot fulfill its mission without the eventual assumption by the state of many functions now performed by individuals and without becoming expressly responsible for an improved distribution of wealth; such changes, however, must be accomplished by purchase on the part of the state or by legitimate use of taxation, not by violent means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits: violent or revolutionary methods to redistribute wealth are condemned as failures. The author emphasizes patience and practicable arrangements; immediate redistributive gains achievable by state action at one time are small, so policy should be incremental and legally grounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve private property while transforming its influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Two indispensable economic conditions of qualitative individual self-expression are (1) the preservation of the institution of private property in some form, and (2) the radical transformation of its existing nature and influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy must balance protection of property rights with reforms that alter how property shapes social and economic power. Evaluations should check both preservation and meaningful transformation rather than abolition or unmodified continuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complement state action with spontaneous individual amelioration
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible state action is necessary but will be wholly vain unless accompanied by a larger measure of spontaneous individual amelioration; the attempt to redeem state responsibilities provides a high type of individuality—viz. the public-spirited man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reform programs should be assessed not only for state measures but for their capacity to stimulate civic virtue and private initiative. Overreliance on state action without cultivating public-spirited individuals is seen as insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject international revolutionary socialism that abolishes nationalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The great weakness of popular forms of socialism lies in their mixture of revolutionary purpose with an international scope; attempts to abolish national distinctions by revolutionary revolt are socially disintegrating and gravely imperil human association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: international socialist programmes that aim to undermine national cohesion. The text argues that national habits and traditions are central bonds of civilized peoples; policies should preserve and develop nationalities rather than attempt supranational class overthrow.

rubrics_metrics.name: National development as a facilitator of democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: If a people, in becoming more of a nation, become for that very reason more of a democracy, then national development provides a simplified, consistent, and practicable programme for achieving the democratic purpose and establishes an alliance between national progress and democratic aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative test: national policies that foster coherent national traditions and institutions may also strengthen democratic commitment. The claim requires historical justification (author promises to show this) and implies that democracy need not require destroying traditional political fabrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty contingent on representative national government
rubrics_metrics.description: The loyalty a citizen owes to a government depends on the extent to which the government is representative of national traditions and organized in the interest of valid national purposes; loyalty does not require uncritical acceptance of national limitations and abuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy legitimacy criterion: governments should be measured by representativeness of national traditions and pursuit of authentic national purposes. Citizens' loyalty is earned by governments that sincerely aim at progressive national interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realize the progressive principle within national ties and official approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The national interest implies devotion to a progressive principle, but that principle must be realized without violating fundamental national ties and must be approved by the official national organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes procedural and normative limits: reforms must respect core national bonds and seek official, constitutional channels of approval rather than illegal or extra-national means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible exercise of national power preserves political efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The political efficiency of states is proportioned to the responsible exercise of their powers; the reckless use of military or state power for undue foreign aggression undermines domestic balance and national loyalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical examples: England's discretion vs. French/Bourbon aggression; Spain's misapplication of military strength. Evaluation: prefer policies that employ state power to secure internal order and national responsibilities rather than futile expansionism.
